title: Cross-sectional momentum across a point-in-time top-20 crypto universe, hourly
hypothesis: Cross-sectional momentum is the one crypto strategy family with substantial published academic support. If nothing in this registry works, this is where a null result is most surprising and most informative. Stated mechanically: Rank the investable universe by trailing return over `lookback` bars; go long the top `entry_threshold` fraction, short the bottom, equal-weighted and dollar-neutral, rebalanced every `holding_cap_bars` bars. Two things make this sweep different from every earlier one in this registry. First, a cross-sectional dollar-neutral portfolio cannot inherit a market trend, so the Bitcoin uptrend that contaminated the time-series crypto results cannot produce an effect here. Second, the universe is rebuilt monthly from the previous month's volume, so coins that later died are held while they lived. Ammann, Burdorf, Liebi and Stockl (SSRN 4287573) measured an annualised survivorship bias of 62.19% for equal-weighted crypto portfolios; taking today's top 20 and backtesting them would make almost any result meaningless.

family_descriptions.xs_momentum: Rank the investable universe by trailing return over `lookback` bars; go long the top `entry_threshold` fraction, short the bottom, equal-weighted and dollar-neutral, rebalanced every `holding_cap_bars` bars.

search_space.enumeration_note: 1 family x 5 lookback x 3 entry_threshold x 1 exit_rule x 3 holding_cap_bars = 45 fully enumerated variants. The mean_touch exit rule, present in SW-0032, is excluded; see supersedes_rationale. No variant is dropped after the fact.

symbols: point-in-time top 20 by prior-month quote volume
data.source: binance public klines via data.binance.vision, see data/manifest/ and data/universe/
data.holdout: 2025-07-01 onward — not loaded or inspected until the verdict is written
data.universe_note: Membership for each month is the top 20 by quote volume over the PREVIOUS month. Delisted pairs remain in the Binance archive and are included for the months in which they actually traded. No symbol is selected using information from after its membership date.

protocol.method: Fixed rules, no in-sample parameter fitting. Equal-weighted and dollar-neutral: the long and short legs are the same size and are drawn only from assets investable in that month. Every variant evaluated over the full period; in-sample/out-of-sample splitting is done by CSCV at scoring time.
protocol.cost_note: 10 bps round trip, against 6 for the single-asset crypto sweeps. Altcoins outside the majors carry materially wider spreads and this strategy rebalances a whole basket, so understating cost here would be the easiest way to manufacture an edge that does not survive contact with an order book.
protocol.execution_model: weights set from bar t close, held over bar t+1, cost charged on the size of every weight change
protocol.survivorship_note: universe rebuilt monthly from prior-month volume; delisted symbols retained for the months they traded
protocol.universe_entry_note: An asset's first bar after entering the universe has its return zeroed: joining the universe is not a price move.

decision_rule.note: Fixed before any result was computed. Not adjustable.

planning.sd_source: n_observations is the assembled panel length, verified against the predecessor's result.json. assumed_var_trial_sharpes is carried over unchanged from the superseded sweep; the realised value could not be re-estimated because the predecessor's returns matrix was produced by the bug this sweep exists to correct. It affects the power calculation only, not the deflated Sharpe ratio or the verdict.

supersedes_rationale:
Replaces SW-0032, voided for a weight-allocation bug in the cross-sectional engine: assets outside the point-in-time universe were scored -inf and sorted first, so the entire short leg of every long_short variant was allocated to non-investable assets with zeroed returns. Fixed in sweep/cross_sectional.py and covered by tests/test_cross_sectional_weights.py. The hypothesis, data, costs and decision rule are unchanged.

One deliberate change to the search space: the mean_touch exit rule is removed. It produces a long-only book at gross exposure 2.0, which is not dollar-neutral and therefore does not test the cross-sectional hypothesis at all. In SW-0032 it inherited the crypto trend and supplied the highest-Sharpe variant, which compounded to a fraction of initial capital with a near-total drawdown despite a positive Sharpe ratio. This exclusion was decided after seeing that result and is recorded as such; it is not a blinded choice. Removing it halves the variant count, which lowers the expected-maximum-Sharpe null and therefore makes the remaining test easier to pass, not harder. That direction is stated here so it cannot be presented later as a tightening.
